slots.practicalActivity: Read through the enterprise-structure, subledger, and Subledger-Accounting/reporting glossary terms and, for any term that still feels fuzzy, go find the real example from your own capstone work (your GRNI journal, your misapplied receipt, your Incomplete transactions) that illustrates it. lessons.title: Functional Interview Questions: Payables and Receivables

slots.practicalActivity: Pick two General Ledger questions and two Payables/Receivables questions from this lesson's lists and record yourself answering each out loud, without reading the model answer first -- pulling real detail from your own capstone work (your chart of accounts design, your GRNI accrual, your misapplied Harborview receipt) instead of a generic textbook answer. slots.deliverable: A written two-paragraph scenario answer using the four-step structure, plus a four-sentence isolate/confirm/fix/document write-up of one real capstone problem.

lessons.title: Technical and Data Questions for Functional Consultants

slots.deliverable: A written one-sentence-per-phase mapping of your capstone onto the five implementation phases, plus a written plain-English explanation of the GL-to-AP reconciliation SQL query.

lessons.title: How to Explain the LTV Manufacturing Capstone in an Interview
Building a Portfolio of Your Practice Work

lessons.title: Certification Study Plan and Practice Habits

slots.practicalActivity: Visit Oracle University's own certification pages for the module you're most interested in (General Ledger, Payables, or Receivables) and write down the current exam name, code, and stated prerequisites directly from Oracle's site -- not a third-party summary. Then mark each of that exam's published objectives as 'covered by my path work,' 'partially familiar,' or 'new to me,' and build a realistic weekly study-session plan (2-3 sessions/week, 45-60 minutes each) around only the last two categories.

lessons.title: Your First 90 Days as an Oracle Financials Consultant
Consulting Career Paths and Next Steps
